name: Yemen
summary: Yemen remains one of the world's worst humanitarian disasters after nearly a decade of civil war. Over 21 million people need humanitarian assistance, with millions facing famine and a collapsed healthcare system battling cholera and other preventable diseases.
context:
Yemen's civil war began in 2014 when Houthi forces seized the capital Sana'a, leading to a Saudi-led military coalition intervention in 2015. The conflict has since devastated the country's infrastructure, economy, and civilian population.

The Saudi-led coalition's aerial bombing campaign has been widely condemned for striking hospitals, schools, markets, and wedding parties. At the same time, Houthi forces have been accused of indiscriminate shelling, child recruitment, and obstructing humanitarian aid delivery.

Yemen was already the poorest country in the Middle East before the war. The conflict has pushed it into catastrophe. The healthcare system has largely collapsed, with fewer than half of health facilities fully functional. Cholera outbreaks have infected over 2.5 million people since 2016 — one of the largest epidemics in modern history.

The port of Hodeidah, through which the majority of Yemen's food and fuel imports pass, has been a flashpoint of the conflict. Blockades and restrictions on imports have directly contributed to famine conditions affecting millions.

Children bear a disproportionate burden of the crisis. UNICEF has called Yemen the worst place on earth to be a child. Malnutrition rates among children under five are among the highest in the world, and an estimated 11 million children need humanitarian assistance.

Despite a fragile truce that began in 2022, the underlying conflict remains unresolved. Peace talks have stalled, and the humanitarian situation continues to deteriorate as international attention and funding decline.

awareness: Share the reality that Yemen has been called the world's worst humanitarian crisis by the UN for multiple years running
Highlight the connection between arms sales to Saudi Arabia and the coalition's bombing campaign in Yemen
Follow and amplify Yemeni journalists, photographers, and aid workers sharing first-hand accounts of the crisis
Organize educational events about Yemen's humanitarian situation — it remains one of the most under-covered crises globally
Share resources about the cholera epidemic and child malnutrition crisis to put a human face on the statistics
political: Demand that your representatives support ending U.S. logistical and intelligence support for the Saudi-led coalition
Advocate for a permanent ceasefire and a resumption of inclusive peace negotiations under UN auspices
Push for an end to the blockade on Yemeni ports that restricts food, fuel, and medical supply imports
Support legislation requiring congressional approval for future arms sales to parties involved in the Yemen conflict
Urge increased funding for the UN humanitarian appeal for Yemen, which has been dramatically underfunded
